word-railway.def: a track made of steel rails for trains, or the whole system of such tracks

word-train-car.def: one of the connected sections that passengers ride in behind the engine

word-conductor.def: an employee who checks tickets and helps passengers on a train

word-ticket-inspector.def: a person whose job is to check that passengers have paid for their journey

word-connection.def: a second bus, train or plane that you change to during a long journey

word-one-way-ticket.def: a pass for going to a place but not coming back again

word-return-ticket.def: a pass that covers going to a place and coming back

word-travel-pass.def: a card that lets you ride buses and trains as often as you like for a set time

word-fare.def: the money you pay to ride a bus, train or plane

word-ticket-machine.def: a device in a station where you pay and get a pass for a journey

word-ticket-office.def: a place in a station where workers sell passes for journeys

word-validate.def: to stamp or scan your paper or card so that you can use it for a journey

word-first-class.def: the most expensive and comfortable section of a plane or train

word-carry-on.def: a small bag that you take with you into the cabin of a plane

word-check-in.def: the process of reporting your arrival at an airport or hotel to get a seat or room

word-boarding-pass.def: a paper or phone screen that lets you get on a plane

word-gate-airport.def: the numbered exit in an airport where you wait to get on your plane

word-terminal.def: a large building at an airport where passengers arrive, leave and wait

word-take-off-plane.def: to leave the ground and begin to fly

word-flight-attendant.def: a worker who serves passengers and keeps them safe on a plane

word-security-check.def: the place at an airport where officers search your bags and look for dangerous items

word-lost-and-found.def: a place where things that people leave behind are kept until their owners come for them

word-travel-agency.def: a business that helps people plan and book vacations and journeys

word-tour-guide.def: a person who shows visitors around a place and explains it to them

word-hostel.def: a cheap place to sleep where travelers often share rooms with other people

word-reception.def: the desk in a hotel where guests arrive, get their keys and ask for help

word-check-out.def: the time or process of paying the bill and leaving a hotel

word-single-room.def: a space in a hotel with a bed for just one guest

word-double-room.def: a space in a hotel with a large bed for two guests

word-ferry.def: a boat that regularly carries people and vehicles across water

word-cruise.def: a vacation on a large ship that visits several ports

word-captain.def: the officer in charge of a ship or plane

word-helicopter.def: an aircraft with spinning blades on top that can rise straight up into the air

word-scooter.def: a light two-wheeled vehicle with a small motor and a platform for your feet

word-hitchhike.def: to travel by standing at the side of the road and asking drivers for a free ride

word-destination.def: the place that someone or something is traveling to

word-route.def: the roads or paths that you follow to get from one place to another

word-rush-hour.def: the time of day when many people are going to or from work and the roads are crowded

word-commute.def: to travel regularly between your home and your workplace

word-jet-lag.def: the tired feeling you get after flying across several time zones

word-sightseeing.def: the activity of visiting famous or interesting places as a tourist

word-guidebook.def: a book with information for visitors about a place

word-accommodation.def: a place where you can stay and sleep while you are away from home

word-backpacker.def: a traveler who carries a pack on their back and spends little money
